nodes.question: How do the survey locations differ among the habitats studied?
nodes.answer: Surveys in disturbed habitat (MH1) were conducted in a disturbed area, while surveys in primary habitat (MH2) were conducted in undisturbed forest locations, and edge habitat (MH3) consists of a secondary habitat with a natural edge.

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What was the purpose of the study mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The study aimed to develop the first regional assessment of habitat suitability and conservation status for Southeast Asia's small felids.
nodes.paragraph: 2021). However, small felids have crucial ecological roles in the trophic structure of ecosystems (Roemer et al. 2009), and some of them can also take on the role of apex predators through ecological release when larger carnivores are extirpated (de Oliveira et al. 2010). Additionally, small felids have been revealed to be important indicator and sentinel species (Chiaverini et al. 2022; Cruz et al. 2019), likely due to their relatively fast rates of population change and to their direct responses to both bottom-up and top-down ecological processes (Marneweck et al. 2022). In this paper we sought to develop the first regional assessment of habitat suitabil- ity and conservation status for Southeast Asia S small felids. By modelling habitat suit- ability individually for seven species of smaller felids (mainland Neofelis nebulosa and Sunda clouded leopards Neofelis diardi, Asiatic golden cat Catopuma temminckii, mar - bled cat Pardofelis marmorata, leopard cat Prionailurus bengalensis, Sunda leopard cat Prionailurus javanensis, and Borneo bay cat Catopuma badia, sampled in three regions (mainland, Borneo and Sumatra) we sought to: (1) predict the geographic distribution of smaller felids in Southeast Asia, (2) evaluate the effectiveness of the current systems of protected areas to preserve suitable habitats for smaller felids, (3) highlight the most suitable areas currently lacking protection and (4) assess whether small felids suitable habitat was highly associated with geographic distribution of broader biodiversity rich- ness in the region.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What has been of interest to naturalists regarding small terrestrial mammals for centuries?
nodes.answer: Naturalists have been interested in the distribution and overall ecology, including the preferred habitats, of small terrestrial mammals for centuries.
nodes.paragraph: Rondini et al. (2011) state that, even for mammals, detailed distribution information is lacking, which hinders conservation efforts. And they argue that fine- resolution distribution data are important for the develop- ment of global conservation strategies for mammals in order to make predictions about its future distribution. (Rondini et al. 2011:2633). Monitoring programs are standard to many species of conservation concern to assess population development. In Europe, an assessment of population trends is mandatory under the Habitats Directive of 1992 (Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora). Some small terres - trial mammals such as, Microtus tatricus, Sicista betulina, S. subtilis, Cricetus cricetus and Muscardinus avellanarius are listed in Annex IV of this Directive and are of special concern. In Germany, many species are protected by the German BNatschG (federal law on nature).
